item.research_question: What is the origin of the CO oxidation activity of Ruthenium nanoparticles (Ru NPs)?
item.material_system: Ruthenium nanoparticles (Ru NPs) with face-centered cubic (fcc) and hexagonal close-packed (hcp) structures
item.processing_route: Chemical reduction methods using Ru(acac)3 and RuCl3 · nH2O as metal precursors, and poly(N-vinyl-2-pyrrolidone) (PVP) as the stabilizing agent
item.test_conditions: High-energy X-ray diffraction experiments at beamline BL04B2 at SPring-8 in Japan, using X-rays of energy 61.46 keV
key_findings: The CO oxidation activity of fcc Ru NPs increases with increasing particle size, despite the decrease in surface area
The lattice parameter of fcc Ru NPs is larger than the theoretical value of fcc Ru bulk and tends to increase with decreasing particle size
The lattice distortion of fcc Ru NPs is nearly independent of particle size, while the lattice distortion of hcp Ru NPs decreases with increasing particle size
The B factor, related to static atomic displacement, increases slightly with particle size for both fcc and hcp Ru NPs
The catalytic activity of fcc Ru NPs is higher than that of hcp Ru NPs for particle sizes larger than 3.5 nm
The lattice distortion and B factor are more correlated to the CO oxidation activity than the domain surface area
For small particles with sizes below 3.5 nm, lattice distortions of the close-packed plane in the hcp Ru NPs are greater than those in the fcc Ru NPs
item.mechanism: The enhancement of the CO oxidation activity in fcc Ru NPs may be caused by an increase in imperfections due to lattice distortions of close-packed planes and static atomic displacements
item.limitations: The study did not assess the direct relation between the structural characterization and CO oxidation activity, as the measurements were performed in a non-reactive gaseous environment
quotes: Enhancement of the CO oxidation activity in fcc Ru NPs may be caused by an increase in imperfections due to lattice distortions of close-packed planes and static atomic displacements

Although these results were obtained through a non-surface sensitive scattering technique, they may hold clues to understanding the higher CO oxidation activity of fcc Ru NPs compared with that of hcp Ru NPs, for sizes larger than 3 nm

records.text: Paper card. Question: What is the origin of the CO oxidation activity of Ruthenium nanoparticles (Ru NPs)?. System: Ruthenium nanoparticles (Ru NPs) with face-centered cubic (fcc) and hexagonal close-packed (hcp) structures. Processing: Chemical reduction methods using Ru(acac)3 and RuCl3 · nH2O as metal precursors, and poly(N-vinyl-2-pyrrolidone) (PVP) as the stabilizing agent. Test conditions: High-energy X-ray diffraction experiments at beamline BL04B2 at SPring-8 in Japan, using X-rays of energy 61.46 keV. Findings: The CO oxidation activity of fcc Ru NPs increases with increasing particle size, despite the decrease in surface area; The lattice parameter of fcc Ru NPs is larger than the theoretical value of fcc Ru bulk and tends to increase with decreasing particle size; The lattice distortion of fcc Ru NPs is nearly independent of particle size, while the lattice distortion of hcp Ru NPs decreases with increasing particle size; The B factor, related to static atomic displacement, increases slightly with particle size for both fcc and hcp Ru NPs; The catalytic activity of fcc Ru NPs is higher than that of hcp Ru NPs for particle sizes larger than 3.5 nm; The lattice distortion and B factor are more correlated to the CO oxidation activity than the domain surface area; For small particles with sizes below 3.5 nm, lattice distortions of the close-packed plane in the hcp Ru NPs are greater than those in the fcc Ru NPs. Mechanism: The enhancement of the CO oxidation activity in fcc Ru NPs may be caused by an increase in imperfections due to lattice distortions of close-packed planes and static atomic displacements. Limitations: The study did not assess the direct relation between the structural characterization and CO oxidation activity, as the measurements were performed in a non-reactive gaseous environment. Quote: "Enhancement of the CO oxidation activity in fcc Ru NPs may be caused by an increase in imperfections due to lattice distortions of close-packed planes and static atomic displacements"
